concepts.decision: Select identity/admission, encryption, segmentation, management, rogue detection, and availability controls for the radio environment.
concepts.definition: Networks using RF or other nonwired media with association, radio, physical-range, and interference considerations.
concepts.failureExample: An attacker associates from outside a facility because radio range and rogue monitoring were ignored.
concepts.label: Wireless Networks

concepts.decision: Use strong enterprise admission where needed, separate guest/IoT/enterprise traffic, secure AP management, and monitor rogue associations.
concepts.definition: IEEE 802.11 wireless LAN technology using access points and association/security mechanisms.
concepts.failureExample: Guest Wi-Fi shares routes with payroll systems through a flat wireless VLAN.
concepts.label: Wifi

concepts.decision: Allow only needed profiles/devices, manage pairing, update firmware, and consider discovery/range exposure.
concepts.definition: Short-range wireless technology for peripheral/device communication with pairing and proximity risks.
concepts.failureExample: An unmanaged paired device receives data after the authorized user leaves.
concepts.label: Bluetooth

concepts.decision: Segment IoT, manage commissioning/keys/firmware, and monitor gateway/control points.
concepts.definition: Low-power mesh wireless technology common in IoT, with coordinator/mesh and device-lifecycle dependencies.
concepts.failureExample: A compromised sensor joins a flat enterprise path through an unprotected gateway.
concepts.label: Zigbee

concepts.decision: Assess carrier trust, device identity, private/public path, data exposure, coverage/fallback, and management.
concepts.definition: Provider-operated mobile access networks with SIM/device identity, radio coverage, carrier, and roaming dependencies.
concepts.failureExample: Loss of carrier service disables a remote safety function with no fallback.
concepts.label: Cellular 4g 5g

concepts.decision: Use when geographic reach justifies latency/cost; plan encryption endpoints, provider trust, availability, and alternate paths.
concepts.definition: Long-distance radio communication via satellite with coverage, provider, latency, weather, and ground-station dependencies.
concepts.failureExample: A latency-sensitive control service fails because satellite delay/jitter was not modeled.
concepts.label: Satellite

concepts.decision: Define origin trust, cache rules, TLS termination, invalidation, logging, data sensitivity, and provider failure behavior.
concepts.definition: Origin-and-edge distribution service that caches/delivers content through provider-operated edge nodes.
concepts.failureExample: Sensitive personalized content is cached or logged at an edge contrary to policy.
concepts.label: Cdn

concepts.decision: Test effective routes and policy after each infrastructure-as-code or provider change.
concepts.definition: Cloud routing/security construct owned jointly by customer configuration and provider infrastructure.
concepts.failureExample: A default route change bypasses an inspection VPC endpoint.
concepts.label: Vpc

concepts.decision: Protect controller/API identities, policy validation, high availability, audit, staged rollout, and rollback.
concepts.definition: Programmable separation of network control and forwarding, often with centralized policy/controller functions.
concepts.failureExample: A controller misconfiguration pushes an allow rule across all sites.
concepts.label: Sdn

concepts.decision: Define edge identity, configuration, data path, update/rollback, telemetry, and physical/provider ownership.
concepts.definition: Compute/enforcement close to users/devices that can reduce latency but distributes trust and management.
concepts.failureExample: An unpatched edge node enforces stale policy close to many clients.
concepts.label: Edge Network

concepts.decision: Broker identity, MFA, device posture, least privilege, time bounds, logging, revocation, and approved paths.
concepts.definition: Controlled connectivity for offsite users/devices/services to organization resources.
concepts.failureExample: A remote VPN user inherits broad internal routing after authentication.
concepts.label: Remote Connectivity

concepts.decision: Define permitted sources/destinations, route, inspection, identity, logs, and fail behavior for inbound and outbound flows.
concepts.definition: Policy and enforcement governing traffic entering or leaving a cloud/network boundary.
concepts.failureExample: Private workloads have unrestricted internet egress despite no intended external dependency.
concepts.label: Ingress Egress Control

concepts.decision: Prefer a broker/jump path when direct broad network reach would exceed the task need.
concepts.definition: An intermediary-controlled route that mediates remote session identity, destination, scope, and evidence.
concepts.failureExample: A direct VPN makes every internal subnet reachable to a contractor.
concepts.label: Brokered Access Path

concepts.decision: Bind cache keys, authorization, routing, and logs to tenant context where data is tenant-specific.
concepts.definition: Separation that prevents one customer/tenant identity, route, cache entry, or policy from affecting another.
concepts.failureExample: A shared cache omits tenant context and returns another tenant’s content.
concepts.label: Tenant Boundary

concepts.decision: Monitor authorized AP inventory/association patterns and investigate impersonation or unapproved radios.
concepts.definition: Detection and response for unauthorized or impersonating wireless access infrastructure.
concepts.failureExample: A rogue AP uses a trusted SSID to collect credentials.
concepts.label: Rogue Access Point Detection

misconceptions.claim: A private cloud subnet is automatically trusted.
misconceptions.correction: Cloud routes, identities, APIs, peering, provider personnel, and misconfiguration still create paths and trust decisions.
Admission, management, endpoint posture, monitoring, and physical radio exposure remain relevant.

outcome: Assess a wireless, cloud, or remote connectivity design for trust boundaries, shared responsibility, resilience, and observable security controls.

sections.body: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Zigbee, satellite, and 4G/5G differ in range, association, identity, encryption, interference, provider dependence, and physical exposure. Select standards and admission controls for the use case, separate guest/IoT/enterprise paths, protect management, monitor rogue devices and unusual associations, and plan loss of carrier or positioning service.
keyPoints: Radio reach crosses physical boundaries and can expose unmanaged clients.
Wireless security includes client, AP, controller, identity, and management paths.
Cellular and satellite add provider and availability dependencies.
sections.title: Design for radio and mobile exposure

sections.body: VPCs, SDN/SD-WAN, NFV, CDNs, peering, ingress/egress, and edge services shift enforcement and routing into programmable or provider-operated layers. Define shared responsibility, tenant boundaries, identity, route controls, encryption endpoints, logging, region/data implications, resilience, and revocation. Remote access should use explicit brokered paths rather than treating a VPN as automatic trust.
keyPoints: Cloud control-plane permissions can change network reachability at scale.
CDN and peering decisions affect origin exposure, data location, and availability.
Provider controls require customer-side configuration, evidence, and exit planning.
sections.title: Govern cloud and remote trust
